review_scope: Exactly the four reconstructed candidates from source reconstruction PR #342.

items.headline: SNAP enrollment drop strains local food pantries
items.historical_date_assignment_basis: The report was published Sep. 1 and describes current local pantry demand and SNAP loss in the Quad Cities service area.
items.geography: Rock Island, Illinois; River Bend Food Bank 23-county service area
affected_groups: children in the River Bend service area
people who lost or could not retain SNAP benefits
items.pressure_type: SNAP benefit access contraction and emergency food demand
items.supporting_passage: KWQC reports food insecurity at a four-year high across the 23-county service area, increased pantry requests, and households reporting that SNAP had stopped.
items.recommended_headline: Illinois food pantries report higher demand as SNAP access falls
items.recommended_summary: A Quad Cities-area food bank reported a four-year high in food insecurity, while a Rock Island pantry reported more people seeking help, including people who said their SNAP benefits had stopped.
items.reason: Concrete Illinois pantry demand and reported SNAP loss are documented. The edited wording attributes the reports and avoids implying that every pantry request was caused by SNAP changes.

items.headline: Worsening hunger crisis pushes North Carolina food insecurity to generational highs
items.historical_date_assignment_basis: The report was published Sep. 2 and describes North Carolina food insecurity and pantry demand using the newly reported Map the Meal Gap analysis.
items.geography: North Carolina, including central and eastern North Carolina
affected_groups: families using pantries and meal sites
items.pressure_type: food insecurity and emergency food network demand surge
items.supporting_passage: WUNC reports food insecurity at a generational high and an unsustainable surge in visits to local pantries and meal sites.
items.recommended_headline: North Carolina pantries report rising demand amid worsening food insecurity
items.recommended_summary: WUNC reported that North Carolina food insecurity had reached a generational high and that local pantries and meal sites were experiencing an unsustainable surge in visits, based on Feeding America analysis.
items.reason: The source ties the demand signal to North Carolina and attributes the generational-high characterization. The edit preserves that attribution and distinguishes this Sep. 2 development from later North Carolina coverage.

items.headline: Hawaii announces automated SNAP replacement after Tropical Cyclone Lala food loss
items.historical_date_assignment_basis: The official release is dated September 2, 2026; the page was posted Sep. 3 and is retained as a later web presentation of the dated release.
items.geography: Hawaii County, City and County of Honolulu, and West Maui; Hawaii, U.S. state
affected_groups: SNAP households affected by Tropical Cyclone Lala
households with storm-related food loss and power outages
items.pressure_type: disaster-related food loss and SNAP replacement access
items.supporting_passage: Hawaii DHS says families experienced food loss from severe weather, prolonged outages, and flooding, and announces automatic replacement benefits plus an extended reporting deadline.
items.recommended_headline: Hawaii DHS announces SNAP replacement for households with cyclone-related food loss
items.recommended_summary: Hawaii DHS said households in Hawaii County, Honolulu, and West Maui affected by Tropical Cyclone Lala could receive automatic replacement of 45% of August SNAP benefits; households outside approved areas or with greater losses could apply through Sep. 13.
items.reason: The official release documents food loss and clearly limits automatic replacement to named areas while distinguishing application-based replacement. The edit prevents the item from reading as a statewide automatic issuance.

items.headline: Texas food banks struggle amid federal cuts and increased demand
items.historical_date_assignment_basis: The report was published Sep. 3 and documents current food-bank demand, rationing, and supply pressure in Texas.
items.geography: Texas, including Houston, rural counties, San Antonio, Central Texas, and the Rio Grande Valley
affected_groups: families using food banks and pantries
rural households dependent on emergency food providers
items.pressure_type: food-bank capacity strain, supply reduction, and SNAP access pressure
items.supporting_passage: The Texas Tribune reports increased demand, dwindling supplies, and food-bank rationing, including reduced distribution frequency and stricter pantry limits.
items.recommended_headline: Texas food banks report rising demand and tighter supplies
items.recommended_summary: The Texas Tribune reported that food banks were facing increased demand and reduced supplies, with some providers rationing food, reducing distribution frequency, or considering stricter visit limits.
items.reason: The source explicitly documents Texas food-bank strain and rationing. The edit keeps the provider reports bounded and avoids presenting statewide uniformity or unsupported causation.
